course_description:
This course will examine contemporary issues in private law. Topics will vary from year to year, drawing on the innovative research of TC Beirne School of Law academic staff, as well as the expertise of visiting scholars and leading practitioners. Please refer to the Law School website for current topics.

A typical range of topics will include issues relating to private and commercial law, such as the law of contract, tort, medical law, property, public body liability, unjust enrichment and restitution, law and technology, sports law, and taxation.

LAWS7721 Topic in Semester 2, 2026 is Advanced Employment Law.

This course examines advanced and contemporary issues in employment law in Australia and beyond, focusing on doctrinal developments arising from recent jurisprudence, emerging regulatory frameworks, and the complex challenges of cross-border employment.

Particular emphasis is placed on the contractual structuring of the employment relationship, evaluating express terms, implied terms, and the legal thresholds for incorporating workplace policies. Students will engage in a cross-jurisdictional comparative analysis of worker status, contrasting Australia’s model for traditional and platform-dependent workers against the systems in the United Kingdom and New Zealand. The course also explores contractual mechanisms used by employers to protect commercial interests across borders, including cascading restraints of trade, non-compete clauses, and extraterritorial provisions.

Additionally, the course investigates contemporary statutory and judicial responses to systemic workplace harm, termination, and emerging technology. Students will evaluate the operational mechanics of the mandatory positive duty to eliminate discrimination, the management of psychosocial hazards, the right to disconnect, workplace surveillance, and work from home (WFH) arrangements. The curriculum considers the legal and commercial complexities of workplace dissolution—ranging from genuine redundancy and business collapse to unfair deactivation for regulated platform workers—alongside strategic legal arguments for adverse action and general protections claims within the Fair Work Commission.

Finally, the course breaks down how workplace disputes are managed in practice. Students are provided with the opportunity to engage in mock oral advocacy using a hypothetical conciliation conference scenario, providing the opportunity to consider claim options and case strategies under pressure.

course_aims:
Education Mission Statement

The mission of the School of Law is to educate you in and about the law. We seek to assist you to think critically about the law and to investigate its structures, principles, policies, and values. This is achieved by engaging with you as fellow investigators in a range of critical and intellectual conversations about the law and its place in society. Our role is thus to guide you in your own intellectual journey in the law and to equip you with the necessary skills that will enable you to continue that journey long after you have left the School.

Course Aims

Refer to objectives below.

learning_outcomes.description: Analyse how the employment relationship is contractually structured, including the legal thresholds for incorporating workplace policies and implied terms into express contracts.
Evaluate how worker status is determined across jurisdictions, contrasting Australia’s text-based binary model with the UK's three-tier framework and New Zealand’s reality-based test.
Assess how employers use cascading restraints of trade, non-compete clauses, and extraterritorial provisions to protect commercial interests and manage cross-border employees.
Formulate strategic legal arguments for adverse action and general protections claims within the statutory architecture and reverse onus frameworks of the Fair Work Commission.
Navigate workplace disputes including considering an employee's protected right to raise complaints, interpersonal misconduct, bullying and sexual harassment.

Critically evaluate how modern regulatory frameworks govern systemic workplace harm, focusing on the mandatory positive duty, psychosocial hazards, workplace surveillance, the right to disconnect and work from home arrangements.
Advise on the legal and commercial complexities of workplace termination, including genuine redundancy, business transfers or collapse, and unfair deactivation for regulated platform workers.
Reflect critically on the advocacy strategies, jurisdictional hurdles, and tactical performance demonstrated within a simulated cross-border dispute.

learning_activities.topic: Day 1 - The Doctrinal Foundations & The Contractualisation of Work • Topic 1: Historical evolution and overview of Australian employment law and international influences. • Topic 2: Distinguishing employment contracts from services contracts • Topic 3: Textual construction of express terms; linguistic thresholds for policy incorporation; implied terms. • Topic 4: Comparative worker status (AU text binary vs. UK three-tier framework vs. NZ reality-based s 6 ERA test). Learning outcomes: L01, L02

Day 2 - Restraints of Trade, Cross-Border Employees: Extraterritoriality, General Protections & ADR in the FWC • Topic 5: Restraints of trade, reasonableness, cascading clauses, and the "blue pencil" rule. • Topic 6: Managing cross-border employees, extraterritorial provisions, and corporate hub friction. • Topic 7: General Protections - Statutory architecture of adverse action, protected workplace rights, the reverse onus of proof, anti-discrimination provisions; Alternative dispute resolution in FWC. Learning outcomes: L03, L04

Day 3 - Bullying, Sexual Harassment, WHS (positive duties and psychosocial hazards), Remedial Damages and Termination – Pt 1 • Topic 8: Bullying and Sexual Harassment under the Fair Work Act 2009 (Cth) • Topic 9: Positive Duties and Management of Psychosocial Hazards • Topic 10: Termination – Pt 1: Lawful Dismissal and Unfair Dismissal Learning outcomes: L05, L06, L07

Day 4 - Termination – Pt 2, Right to Disconnect, Workplace Surveillance, & WFH Arrangements • Topic 11: Termination – Pt 2 (Genuine redundancy; Redundancy payments; Transfer of business; Business collapse; Unfair deactivation for regulated workers) • Topic 12: The right to disconnect, "reasonable refusal" of contact, workplace surveillance and work from home arrangements Learning outcomes: L06, L07
